frames.narration: A request arrives with API key k_42. The gateway has to decide before it touches the API.
The gateway reads the key's plan limit from its local copy of the rules: 100 requests per minute. No network call is needed for this.
It hashes the key to find the right counter shard and sends one atomic command: take a token for k_42, using the shard's own clock.
The bucket has tokens left, so the shard allows it and reports how many remain.
The gateway forwards the request to the API, and adds the remaining quota to the response headers.
Later the same key runs out. The shard answers 'denied' and says when a token will be free.
The gateway answers 429 with Retry-After: 3. The API never saw the request, so a flood of rejected calls costs it nothing.
If the shard were unreachable, calls would time out, the circuit breaker would open, and the gateway would use its local fallback limit instead of blocking or allowing everything.
